result.note: Official CPI data release; tested the April 2026 print against forecast and the reason it stayed low, avoiding the speculative FY27 outlook.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about India's retail inflation data for April 2026, released in May 2026:
items: Retail inflation came in above the forecast of 3.8%.
The print was held down because the Centre absorbed most of the oil price shock instead of raising prices at the pump.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Retail inflation rose to 3.48%, below the 3.8% forecast, so statement 1 is wrong. The Centre's decision to absorb the oil shock kept fuel prices steady, though food inflation climbed to 4.2%.
questions.source: India's retail inflation rose to 3.48% in April, undershooting the 3.8% forecast, as the Centre absorbed most of the oil price shock rather than raising prices at the pump.
